blocks.text: I can describe the weather in summer.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Weather is what the conditions are like in a particular place at a particular time. For example, rain, wind or sun.
Seasons are periods of similar weather. In the UK there are four seasons (spring, summer, autumn and winter).
Summer is the season after spring and before autumn.
Temperature is how hot or cold something is.
A thermometer is a piece of equipment for measuring temperature.

blocks.text: Laura says each month has different weather.
Lucas says the weather is different in each season.
The weather is often different in each season, not in every month.

items.title: spring
items.sub: Mixed. Cold, windy, rainy and sometimes sunny and warm.

items.title: winter
items.sub: Cold, windy and rainy. Fog, frost or snow too.

blocks.text: It is the last day of term in July.
July is in summer.
Lucas says it is really hot. The sky looks blue.
Summer comes after spring and the weather turns warmer. Summer is usually the warmest season.
Summer is usually the warmest season.
But the weather is not always warm and sunny.
It can be cloudy, cool and rainy.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: It is summer, but it is cool today. One child wears a jumper.
Sometimes there are lots of very hot days in a row.
This is called a {heatwave}.

blocks.q: Which weather can happen in summer?

items.q: Which season is usually the warmest in the UK?
It is July and the weather is cool and rainy. Is that possible?
options: No. It is always hot in summer.
Yes. Summer can be cloudy, cool and rainy.

items.title: shorts
items.sub: Izzy wears shorts instead of trousers.

items.title: water
items.sub: She needs a drink to cool down.

items.title: shade
items.sub: Laura stays in the shade. Her face looks red.

blocks.text: It has been hot. There has not been much rain.
The ground is very dry.
Some of the grass has died.
The soil is cracked because it is so dry.

items.title: a fan
items.sub: It is cooler inside with a fan on.

items.title: t-shirt and shorts
items.sub: Clothes that help you stay cool.

items.title: a cap
items.sub: It helps to protect your face from the sun.

items.title: flip flops
items.sub: You can wear them when not at school.

blocks.text: How can Izzy check how hot it is?
**Temperature** is how hot or cold something is.
A **thermometer** is a piece of equipment for measuring temperature.
We can use it to measure the temperature of the weather in different seasons.

items: A thermometer has numbers on it.
Read the number next to the top of the coloured line.
The higher the number, the hotter it is.
Some thermometers show a number, like a digital clock.

blocks.label: An example
blocks.text: Three thermometers show 24, 18 and 30 degrees. The one that shows 30 is the hottest.

items.q: Three thermometers show 12, 27 and 21 degrees. Which is the hottest?
Monday was 26 degrees. Tuesday was 19 degrees. Which day was warmer?
Where do you read the temperature on a thermometer with a coloured line?
options: next to the top of the coloured line
at the bottom of the thermometer

blocks.text: One week in summer, the temperature was:

blocks.label: Which day was the warmest?
blocks.text: Friday, at 26 degrees. Wednesday was the coolest, at 14 degrees.

items: The weather is often different in each season.
Summer is the warmest season in the UK, but it can still be windy and rainy.
Temperature is how hot or cold something is.
A thermometer can be used to measure the temperature of different seasons.

flashcards.front: Is the weather the same in every season?
flashcards.back: No. The weather is often different in each season.

flashcards.front: Which season is usually the warmest in the UK?
Summer comes after which season, and before which season?
Can it be windy and rainy in summer?
flashcards.back: Yes. Summer is usually warm, but it can be cloudy, cool and rainy too.

flashcards.front: What is it called when there are lots of very hot days in a row?

flashcards.back: A guess or prediction about the weather.
How hot or cold something is.
A piece of equipment for measuring temperature.

flashcards.front: How do you read a thermometer with a coloured line?
flashcards.back: Read the number next to the top of the coloured line.

flashcards.front: On a thermometer, what does a higher number mean?
Name two things that can happen to a person in very hot weather.
flashcards.back: They feel very warm and sweat. They need to drink water.

flashcards.front: What does the ground look like after hot weather with not much rain?
flashcards.back: Very dry. Some grass dies and the soil is cracked.

flashcards.front: Name clothes that help you stay cool in hot, sunny weather.
flashcards.back: A t-shirt and shorts. A cap protects your face from the sun.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Weather in summer
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word, a number or a short answer.

questions.prompt: Which season is usually the warmest in the UK?
questions.explanation: Summer is the warmest season in the UK.

questions.prompt: What do we call how hot or cold something is?
questions.explanation: Temperature is how hot or cold something is.

questions.prompt: What do we use to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer is a piece of equipment for measuring temperature.

questions.prompt: What is it called when there are lots of very hot days in a row?
questions.explanation: Lots of very hot days in a row is called a heatwave.

questions.prompt: Three thermometers show 12, 27 and 21 degrees. Which is the hottest? Write the number.
questions.explanation: The higher the number, the hotter it is, and 27 is the highest.

questions.prompt: Monday was 26 degrees and Tuesday was 19 degrees. Which day was warmer?
questions.explanation: 26 is higher than 19, so Monday was warmer.

questions.prompt: True or false? The weather in summer is always sunny.
questions.explanation: Summer is usually the warmest season, but it can still be cloudy, cool, windy and rainy.

questions.prompt: What do we call a guess about tomorrow’s weather?
questions.explanation: When we try to guess or predict the weather, it is called a forecast.
